# Presets

A preset is a configuration that says where its criterion comes from. Use them in `extends`; later ones
win, and each is applied once. `crowded-folders init` proposes the ones that fit a repository, and
`crowded-folders presets` lists them in the terminal.

Where a guide gives a number, the preset uses it and quotes it. Where none does — most of them — the
limits are the ones measured over 36 real repositories ([field-trial.md](field-trial.md)): 20 modules is
about the median 95th percentile of folder sizes (19), the biggest folder in twenty.

| Preset | Proposed by `init` |
| --- | --- |

## recommended

The two rules that matter, at limits measured on real repositories: at most 20 modules in a folder (a module is a file with its companions: foo.ts, foo.spec.ts and foo.html are one), and 4 modules sharing a first word make a folder. Leaves out vendored, generated and test-data folders, changelog fragments, media, translations and the folders of tools (.github). Migrations are left out by their name as well as by their folder (Flyway V1__init.sql, golang-migrate 000001_x.up.sql), and so are fastlane/metadata and the usual names of generated code (__generated__, *.generated.*). The root of every package (a folder with package.json, go.mod, Cargo.toml…) gets the 40 of the repository root, scripts/ and tooling/ read validate-i18n as being about i18n, and __tests__ and stories follow the code they sit next to: a problem of both is reported once, in the code, and its moves take the tests along. The .patch files in a patches/ folder stay where they are: patch-package reads them there, by name.

- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","dotfiles":false}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"min":4,"words":1,"ignore":["test","tests","spec","get","set","is","has","can","should"]}`
- **`max-folders`:** `off`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `off`
- **`single-file-folders`:** `off`
- **`case-collision`:** `off`
- **`scattered-feature`:** `off`
- **`orphan-companions`:** `off`
- **`type-folders`:** `off`
- **Left out:** `node_modules`, `/vendor`, `third_party`, `third-party`, `*[fF]ixtures`, `__fixtures__`, `__snapshots__`, `[sS]napshots`, `[sS]creenshots`, `[gG]oldens`, `[eE]xpected`, `[tT]est[dD]ata`, `__mocks__`, `changelog`, `changelog.d`, `changelog_unreleased`, `newsfragments`, `.*`, `*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf,riv,lottie,caf,aiff,heic,glb,gltf,fbx,obj,tga,ktx2}`, `**/fastlane/metadata`, `migrations`, `**/db/migrate`, `**/alembic/versions`, `**/db/migration`, `{V,U}[0-9]*__*`, `R__*`, `*.{up,down}.sql`, `[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]*[_-]*.{sql,ts,js,mjs,cjs,php,rb,py,cs,exs}`, `__generated__`, `*.generated.*`, `/generated`, `/gen`, `**/src/generated`, `**/src/gen`, `dist`, `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `.git`
- **In `**/locales`, `**/locale`, `**/i18n`, `**/l10n`, `**/translations`, `**/lang`, `**/langs`, `**/[lL]ocali[sz]ation`, `**/[lL]ocali[sz]ation/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Translations are one file per language, side by side by nature: en, en-GB and en-US are not a group to move.
- **In `**/scripts`, `**/scripts/**`, `**/tooling`, `**/tooling/**`, `**/bin`, `**/bin/**`:** . Scripts are named after the verb they run and the thing they run it on (validate-i18n, check-links): the thing is what they are about, not the verb.
- **In `**/__tests__`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/__stories__`, `**/__stories__/**`, `**/stories`, `**/stories/**`:** `prefix-groups` `off`. Tests and stories mirror the code they are next to: when the code is split into folders they follow it, so the group is reported once, in the code.
- **In `.`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`. The root holds what tools look for there on their own: manifests, lockfiles, licences, configs.
- **In `**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`. The root of a package holds what its tools look for, like the root of the repository: the same 25 config files pass in the root and would fail in apps/shop.

Sources:

- [Angular style guide: "consider splitting further"](https://angular.dev/style-guide#project-structure)
- [Flyway: versioned migrations are named like V001.002__NewTwitterColumn.sql, repeatable ones R__SetDefaults.sql](https://documentation.red-gate.com/flyway/flyway-concepts/migrations/versioned-migrations)
- [golang-migrate: {version}_{title}.up.{extension} and {version}_{title}.down.{extension}](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/master/MIGRATIONS.md)

- [Relay: "ahead-of-time compilation of GraphQL queries and fragments to generate artifacts" (kept in __generated__ folders)](https://relay.dev/docs/guides/compiler/)
- [patch-package: "patches are applied from the patches directory", named package-name+version.patch](https://github.com/ds300/patch-package#readme)
- [Jest: test files in __tests__ folders, next to the code they test](https://jestjs.io/docs/configuration#testmatch-arraystring)
- [docs/presets.md: how the limits were measured](https://github.com/bymaksym/CrowdedFolders/blob/main/docs/presets.md)

## strict

Tighter than recommended: at most 12 modules in a folder, 3 modules sharing a prefix make a folder, at most 20 subfolders, no module repeating its folder's name, no folder holding a single file, and no two names that differ only in case. It tightens the presets it is combined with, wherever it is listed (go then strict and strict then go are the same), and leaves alone what a preset keeps: java and dotnet keep redundant-prefix off, go's main.go and Cargo's lib.rs stay allowed alone in a folder. An opinion, not a measurement: use it when you want the tree tidier than most.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":12,"count":"modules"}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"min":3}`
- **`max-folders`:** `error` `{"max":20}`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `error`
- **`single-file-folders`:** `warn`
- **`case-collision`:** `error`

Sources:

- [Angular style guide (former LIFT "Flat" rule: sub-folders at seven or more files)](https://github.com/kenny-chow-my/AngularStyleGuide)

## angular

Angular's own guide: folders by feature, a component's files together, and sub-folders as a folder grows. The current guide gives no number ("consider splitting further"), so a folder of src/ has recommended's measured 20; under features/ the 10 of the former guide stays, which asked for sub-folders from seven files: an opinion, there is no current source for it. Counts a component and its template, styles and spec once. The hint is about TypeScript, so a folder of SCSS partials or images does not get it, and a folder that is already by type (utils/, services/) is told to group by topic inside, not to make features. Scripts and tooling outside src/ keep recommended's limit and no hint.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"dropPrefix":false}`
- **Left out:** `.angular`, `src/environments`
- **In `**/src`, `**/src/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"hint":"Angular asks for folders by feature, not by type (no components/ or services/).","hintFor":["*.ts"]}`. The style guide is about the application code, which Angular puts in src/: "All of your Angular UI code (TypeScript, HTML, and styles) should live inside a directory named src".
- **In `**/src/**/components`, `**/src/**/services`, `**/src/**/utils`, `**/src/**/helpers`, `**/src/**/models`, `**/src/**/types`, `**/src/**/interfaces`, `**/src/**/enums`, `**/src/**/constants`, `**/src/**/pipes`, `**/src/**/directives`, `**/src/**/guards`, `**/src/**/interceptors`, `**/src/**/resolvers`:** `max-files` `error` `{"hint":"This folder is already by type: group by topic inside, e.g. utils/filters/."}`. A folder that is already by type cannot be told to become a feature: what helps is grouping by topic inside it.
- **In `**/src/**/features`, `**/src/**/features/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":10}`. The 10 of the former guide, which asked for sub-folders early ("Flat": seven or more files), kept where the guide's feature folders are.

Sources:

- [Angular style guide: project structure, "As the number of files in a directory grows, consider splitting further into additional sub-directories"](https://angular.dev/style-guide)
- [Former Angular style guide, 04-04 "Flat": sub-folders at seven or more files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/17.3.x/aio/content/guide/styleguide.md)

## react

React has no official layout, so this is recommended plus what React names mean: `use` starts every hook and `with` many higher-order components, so they are skipped before reading what a file is about (useAuthLogin and AuthForm are both about auth). Counts a component with its test, story and styles once.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Leading words skipped:** `use`, `with`
- **Left out:** `public`

Sources:

- [React docs (legacy): file structure — "don't overthink it", at most three or four levels](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/faq-structure.html)
- [React: hook names must start with use](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks)
- [bulletproof-react: project structure by feature](https://github.com/alan2207/bulletproof-react/blob/master/docs/project-structure.md)

## nextjs

React, plus the App Router: under app/ a folder is a URL segment, so the advice is a private folder (_name) or a route group ((name)), which group files without changing URLs.

- **Extends:** [react](#react)
- **Left out:** `.next`, `next-env.d.ts`
- **In `app`, `app/**`, `src/app`, `src/app/**`:** `prefix-groups` `error` `{"hint":"Under app/ a folder is a URL segment: use a private folder (_name) or a route group ((name))."}`. Under the App Router a plain folder becomes part of the URL.

Sources:

- [Next.js: project structure, private folders and route groups](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)

## react-native

React, plus the native projects: ios/ and android/ next to the app are the Xcode and Gradle projects that the template or Expo prebuild generates, not code arranged by hand, so they are left out wherever the app lives in the repository. The _layout, +html, +not-found and +native-intent files of Expo Router describe their folder and do not count. Under the app/ of Expo Router a file is a route, so strict does not ask to flatten a folder whose only file is index or a [param] (experiences/[id].tsx): moving it changes the address. For the same reason a group of screens there (sign-in, sign-up, sign-out) moves into a route group, (sign)/, with its names, which keeps every address.

- **Extends:** [react](#react)
- **`single-file-folders`:** `off` `{"allowed":["**/app/**/index.*","**/app/**/[[]*].*"]}`
- **Left out:** `/ios`, `/android`, `.expo`
- **In `app`, `app/**`, `src/app`, `src/app/**`:** . Expo Router: under app/ the path of a file is its address, so /sign-in must not become /sign/in; a route group, (sign)/, groups screens without changing it.

Sources:

- [Expo Router: "an index.tsx file indicates the default route for a directory"; square brackets in a file or directory name are a dynamic route](https://docs.expo.dev/router/basics/notation/)
- [Expo: continuous native generation — prebuild "creates the android and ios directories"](https://docs.expo.dev/workflow/continuous-native-generation/)
- [Expo Router: notation (_layout, +html, +not-found, [param], (group))](https://docs.expo.dev/router/basics/notation/)

## vue

Vue's style guide asks for the opposite of prefix-groups in components/: tightly coupled children are named after their parent (TodoList, TodoListItem, TodoListItemButton) and kept flat, and sub-folders wait until about 100 components. So components/ gets no prefix groups and a high limit; Base, App and V are skipped as the prefixes of base components.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules"}`
- **Leading words skipped:** `base`, `app`, `v`, `the`, `use`
- **Left out:** `.nuxt`, `.output`
- **In `**/components`, `**/components/**`:** `prefix-groups` `off`, `max-files` `error` `{"max":100}`. The Vue style guide names coupled children after their parent and keeps them flat ("This isn't recommended" about nesting them), and only suggests sub-folders in "very large apps (e.g. 100+ components)".

Sources:

- [Vue style guide: tightly coupled component names, base component names, order of words](https://vuejs.org/style-guide/rules-strongly-recommended.html)

## nuxt

Vue, plus Nuxt's directories: composables/ and utils/ are auto-imported from their top level only, so a sub-folder there breaks imports unless it is re-exported, and in pages/ and server/ a file is a URL. Groups there are warnings that say so.

- **Extends:** [vue](#vue)
- **In `**/composables`, `**/utils`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Nuxt only auto-imports the top level here: a sub-folder needs an index that re-exports it, or imports.dirs in nuxt.config."}`. Nuxt auto-imports only the top level of composables/ and utils/: a file moved into a sub-folder stops being imported, silently.
- **In `**/pages`, `**/pages/**`, `**/server/api`, `**/server/api/**`, `**/server/routes/**`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Here a folder is part of the URL: moving a file changes its route."}`. In pages/ and server/ the path of a file is its URL, so grouping files into a folder changes their routes.

Sources:

- [Nuxt: composables, "Nuxt only scans files at the top level of the app/composables/ directory"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/app/composables)
- [Nuxt: utils, scanned "identical to the app/composables/ directory"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/app/utils)
- [Nuxt: server, "Files inside the ~~/server/api are automatically prefixed with /api in their route"](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/directory-structure/server)

## svelte

Recommended, plus SvelteKit routes: under src/routes a folder is a route, so the advice is a group folder ((name)). The + of route files (+page, +layout) is not a prefix.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `.svelte-kit`, `static`
- **In `src/routes`, `src/routes/**`:** `prefix-groups` `error` `{"hint":"Under src/routes a folder is a route: use a group folder ((name)) to keep the URLs."}`. Under src/routes a plain folder becomes a route.

Sources:

- [SvelteKit: project structure](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/project-structure)
- [SvelteKit: routing (+ files, groups)](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/routing)

## nestjs

NestJS organises by module, one folder per feature (cats/cats.controller.ts, cats/cats.service.ts are one module). Recommended with modules counted once.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"hint":"NestJS groups a feature as a module folder."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"dropPrefix":false}`

Sources:

- [NestJS: modules](https://docs.nestjs.com/modules)

## python

Recommended, read the way pytest names tests: test_parser.py and parser_test.py are the module parser, and __init__.py, which is the package itself, does not count. tests/ mirrors the package, so it is not asked to group on its own — split the package and the tests follow. A move names the package in snake_case, as PEP 8 asks, and never after a keyword: async_* goes to asyncs/, not to an async/ no import can name.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Companions:** `^test_`, `_test$`, `_tests$`
- **Left out:** `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.tox`, `.nox`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `*.egg-info`
- **In `tests`, `tests/**`, `**/tests`, `**/tests/**`:** `prefix-groups` `off`. Tests mirror the package they test: when the package splits, they follow it.

Sources:

- [PEP 8: package and module names](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/)
- [Python: keywords](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#keywords)
- [pytest: good practices, test discovery (test_*.py or *_test.py)](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/goodpractices.html)

## django

Python, plus Django: each app keeps models.py, views.py, admin.py… side by side by convention, and migrations stay flat and numbered (Django's answer to too many is squashing, not folders). management/commands and templatetags stay flat too (the file name is the command, the module the tag library), and templates/ keeps the <app>/<model>_list.html names ListView looks for.

- **Extends:** [python](#python)
- **Left out:** `/static`, `/media`, `/staticfiles`, `**/management/commands`, `**/templatetags`
- **In `**/templates/**`:** `redundant-prefix` `off`. ListView looks for orders/templates/orders/order_list.html by default (<app>/<model>_list.html): the name repeats the folder because Django asks for it.

Sources:

- [Django: applications](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/ref/applications/)
- [Django: migrations (squashing)](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/migrations/)
- [Django: custom management commands (management/commands/<name>.py, run as manage.py <name>)](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/howto/custom-management-commands/)
- [Django: custom template tags (a templatetags package in the app)](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/howto/custom-template-tags/)

## go

Go puts a package in a folder, and a new folder is a new package with its own API — so the limits are looser and the advice is about packages. Reads foo_test.go, foo_linux.go and foo_linux_amd64_test.go as foo, and does not count doc.go, the package comment. Go's own guidance: "There is no 'one type, one file' convention"; net/http has 17 files and the go command 34. A move proposes a package as Go names them, lowercase in one word (httpserver/), never a keyword.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules","hint":"In Go a folder is a package: split off a part that has its own API, not just to shorten the list.","hintFor":["*.go"]}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"hint":"In Go a folder is a package: would they make sense as their own package?","hintFor":["*.go"]}`
- **`single-file-folders`:** `off` `{"allowed":["main.go"]}`
- **Companions:** `_test$`, `_(aix|android|darwin|dragonfly|freebsd|hurd|illumos|ios|js|linux|nacl|netbsd|openbsd|plan9|solaris|wasip1|windows|zos|unix)$`, `_(386|amd64|arm|arm64|loong64|mips|mipsle|mips64|mips64le|ppc64|ppc64le|riscv64|s390x|sparc64|wasm)$`
- **Left out:** `testdata`, `*.pb.go`, `*_string.go`, `zz_generated.*`, `mock_*.go`, `wire_gen.go`, `*_templ.go`, `*.sql.go`, `*.pb.gw.go`

Sources:

- [Go: organizing a Go module: multiple programs in the same repository will typically have separate directories (prog1/main.go)](https://go.dev/doc/modules/layout)
- [Google Go style: package size](https://google.github.io/styleguide/go/best-practices)
- [The Go blog: organizing Go code](https://go.dev/blog/organizing-go-code)
- [The Go blog: package names are lowercase, single-word](https://go.dev/blog/package-names)
- [The Go specification: keywords](https://go.dev/ref/spec#Keywords)
- [go build: _test.go, testdata and build constraints in file names](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go)

## rust

Recommended for Rust: render_json.rs and render_pr.rs become render.rs and render/json.rs, the module layout the Rust reference prefers, so a move leaves render.rs where it is, names the folder in snake_case and never after a keyword (type/, mod/ and match/ would need r#). mod.rs, the module of the folder itself, does not count. Cargo builds one target per file in src/bin, examples, benches and tests, so those stay flat.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`single-file-folders`:** `off` `{"allowed":["lib.rs","main.rs"]}`
- **Left out:** `/target`
- **In `**/src/bin`, `**/examples`, `**/benches`, `**/tests`, `**/tests/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Cargo makes every file there its own target (binary, example, benchmark, integration test), and UI-test suites keep one case per file.

Sources:

- [The Rust reference: modules and module source files](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/modules.html)
- [Cargo: package layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/project-layout.html)
- [The Rust reference: keywords](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/keywords.html)
- [Rust API guidelines: modules are snake_case](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/naming.html)

## java

Java and Kotlin with Maven or Gradle: a folder is a package, so groups of classes sharing a name (UserService, UserRepository, UserController) suggest packaging by feature. UserServiceImpl is UserService, and in test sources UserServiceTest and UserServiceIT are too; AbstractUserService, DefaultUserService and FakeUserService are about user; package-info.java and module-info.java describe the package and do not count; and a build/ or target/ is left out only next to the pom.xml or build.gradle that owns it (com/acme/build is a package). A move proposes a package as Java writes them (registrohorario/, never a keyword such as abstract/), keeps the class names, takes src/test along with src/main, and leaves the application-{profile}.yml of Spring where Spring looks for them. One top-level class per file makes folders larger than in TypeScript, hence 20: across five Java repositories (docs/field-trial.md) the 95th percentile of modules per folder is 9 to 32, median 11.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","hint":"A folder is a package: package by feature (user/, order/), not by layer.","hintFor":["*.{java,kt,kts,groovy,scala}"]}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"A folder is a package: they would be the package of that feature.","hintFor":["*.{java,kt,kts,groovy,scala}"],"dropPrefix":false}`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `off`
- **Companions:** `Impl$`
- **Leading words skipped:** `fake`, `mock`, `stub`, `spy`, `dummy`, `abstract`, `base`, `default`, `simple`
- **Left out:** `/target`, `/build`, `.gradle`, `META-INF`
- **In `**/src/test`, `**/src/test/**`, `**/src/*Test`, `**/src/*Test/**`:** . A test class is named after the class it tests (UserServiceTest, UserServiceIT), and only in test sources: elsewhere SpeedTest and AuditIT are names of their own.
- **In `**/build-logic`, `**/build-logic/**`, `**/buildSrc`, `**/buildSrc/**`:** . Convention plugins are named after the platform they configure (AndroidApplicationConventionPlugin, AndroidLibraryConventionPlugin): the platform is not what they are about.

Java/Kotlin, plus Android resources: res/ folders cannot have sub-folders ("Alternative resource directories can't be nested"), so prefixes such as activity_, fragment_ and ic_ are the only grouping there is. res/ and the composeResources/ of Kotlin Multiplatform (the same fixed layout: drawable, font, values, files) are left out, and Platform.kt, Platform.android.kt and Platform.ios.kt are one module, as the Kotlin conventions name them.

- **Extends:** [java](#java)
- **Left out:** `**/src/*/res`, `/res`, `**/src/*/composeResources`

## dotnet

C# and .NET: a folder is a namespace (IDE0130 is on by default), the I of an interface is not what it is about (IUserService belongs with UserService), FakeUserService is about user, and in test projects UserServiceTests is UserService. One type per file, hence 20. A move proposes the folder in PascalCase, as the namespace is written, and keeps the file names, which are the type names.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules","hint":"In C# a folder is a namespace (IDE0130).","hintFor":["*.{cs,fs,vb}"]}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"In C# a folder is a namespace (IDE0130).","hintFor":["*.{cs,fs,vb}"],"dropPrefix":false}`
- **`redundant-prefix`:** `off`
- **Companions:** `^I(?=[A-Z])`
- **Leading words skipped:** `i`, `fake`, `mock`, `stub`, `spy`, `dummy`
- **Left out:** `bin`, `obj`, `Migrations`, `wwwroot/lib`, `Properties`, `.vs`
- **In `**/*Tests`, `**/*Tests/**`, `**/*Test`, `**/*Test/**`, `**/tests`, `**/tests/**`:** . A test class is named after the class it tests (UserServiceTests), and only in test projects: elsewhere SpeedTest is a class of its own.

Sources:

- [IDE0130: namespace does not match folder structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/style-rules/ide0130)
- [Names of namespaces: PascalCase](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/names-of-namespaces)
- [C# keywords](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/)
- [C# identifier names: interfaces start with I](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/coding-style/identifier-names)

## swift

Asset catalogs, localisation folders, Xcode bundles, vendored frameworks (.xcframework, .framework, .bundle) and DocC resources are left out.

- **In `**/*Tests`, `**/*Tests/**`:** . A test case is named after the type it tests (UserTests), and only in test targets: elsewhere SpeedTest and ABTest are types of their own.

## flutter

Flutter and Dart: feature-first under lib/ui, foo_test.dart is foo, and the generated platform folders and localisation files are left out. Flutter's own architecture guide organises lib/data by type on purpose, so it is given more room. main.dart and its flavours (main_dev.dart, main_prod.dart) stay where flutter run -t looks for them, and a move keeps the file names (auth/auth_repository.dart, as the guide names them) in a snake_case folder.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"dropPrefix":false}`
- **Companions:** `_test$`
- **Left out:** `.dart_tool`, `/build`, `/android`, `/ios`, `/web`, `/windows`, `/linux`, `/macos`, `**/lib/l10n`, `**/lib/generated`, `*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`, `*.gr.dart`, `*.mocks.dart`, `*.config.dart`, `*.gen.dart`, `*.pb*.dart`, `*.chopper.dart`, `*.arb`
- **In `lib/data/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":30}`, `prefix-groups` `warn`. The Flutter architecture guide organises the data layer by type: "The data folder organizes code by type".

## rails

Ruby on Rails organises app/ by type by design, and every sub-folder is a Zeitwerk namespace (app/models/admin/role.rb is Admin::Role): app/models, controllers, jobs, mailers and helpers get more room, and groups there are warnings that suggest a namespace. user_test.rb and user_spec.rb are user, and spec/ and test/ mirror app/: a problem of both is reported once, in app/, and its moves take the specs along.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`
- **Companions:** `_(test|spec)$`
- **Left out:** `/tmp`, `/log`, `/storage`, `/public`, `app/assets/builds`, `db/schema.rb`
- **In `app/{models,controllers,jobs,mailers,helpers,policies,serializers,services,workers,validators,presenters}`, `app/{models,controllers,jobs,mailers,helpers,policies,serializers,services,workers,validators,presenters}/**`, `app/views/**`, `spec/**`, `test/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`, `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"In Rails a sub-folder is a namespace (Render::Json).","hintFor":["*.rb"]}`. Rails sorts these by type on purpose, and a sub-folder is a namespace that changes every constant in it.

Sources:

- [Rails guides: autoloading and namespaces (Zeitwerk)](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/autoloading_and_reloading_constants.html)

## php

PHP with Composer (Laravel, Symfony): a folder is a PSR-4 namespace and there is one class per file, hence 20. Laravel sorts app/Models and app/Http/Controllers by type, so they get more room. UserTest is User. A move proposes the folder in PascalCase, as the namespace is written, and keeps the file names, which are the class names.

## elixir

Elixir and Phoenix: mix phx.gen.html writes user_controller.ex, user_html.ex and user_json.ex (and user_controller_test.exs) for one resource, and they are one module, user. The limits are recommended's measured 20: no Elixir guide gives a number. _build, deps and the compiled assets are left out. test/ mirrors lib/: a problem of both is reported once, in lib/, and its moves take the tests along.

## c-cpp

C and C++: foo.h, foo.cc and foo_test.cc are one module. Without namespaces in C, a shared prefix is often the subsystem's name on purpose (Google: "http_server_logs.h rather than logs.h"), so groups are warnings and need five. Generated Qt and protobuf files are left out.

## unity

Unity: every asset has a .meta next to it (Player.cs and Player.cs.meta are one), Scripts.meta goes with the folder Scripts/, numbered series such as Model1, Model_2 are one asset family (in Scripts/ only with a separator: Base64.cs is not Base), and Library, Temp, ProjectSettings (one .asset per setting, written by Unity) and third-party code (Plugins, TextMesh Pro, Samples, ThirdParty) are left out. The manifest files of Packages/ are left out, the embedded packages in it are your code and are checked. C# reads as in the dotnet preset. The Unity guide splits by asset type and gives no number: the 15 for groups is borrowed from the Allar guide for Unreal and is an opinion here. A .meta without its asset is an error (orphan-companions): the Unity manual says a .meta "must stay with the asset file", and the .meta of an empty folder, which git cannot store, is not reported.

- **Extends:** [dotnet](#dotnet)
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":15,"hint":"Unity's guide splits a project by asset type and gives no number: the 15 is borrowed from Allar's Unreal guide (rule 2.7) and is an opinion here.","hintFor":["!*.{cs,fs,vb}"]}`
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":30,"count":"modules"}`
- **`orphan-companions`:** `error`
- **Companions:** `_?\d+$`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf,riv,lottie,caf,aiff,heic,glb,gltf,fbx,obj,tga,ktx2}`, `/Library`, `/Temp`, `/Logs`, `/UserSettings`, `/ProjectSettings`, `/Packages/*.json`, `Assets/Plugins`, `Assets/TextMesh Pro`, `Assets/Samples`, `Assets/ThirdParty`, `*~`
- **In `**/Scripts`, `**/Scripts/**`:** . A script is named after its type, and a number there is part of the name: Base64, Sha256 and Md5 are not copies of Base, Sha and Md. Only a separated number (Spawner_2) is a copy.

Sources:

- [Unity manual: asset metadata (.meta files)](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/AssetMetadata.html)
- [Unity manual: special folder names](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/SpecialFolders.html)
- [Unity manual: embedding a package in a project (Packages/<name>)](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/upm-embed.html)
- [Allar's UE5 style guide, rule 2.7: the number 15 is borrowed from it, Unity's guide gives none](https://github.com/Allar/ue5-style-guide)
- [Unity: best practices for organizing your project](https://unity.com/how-to/organizing-your-project)

## unreal

Unreal Engine, after Allar's style guide: an asset is named Prefix_BaseAssetName_Variant_Suffix, the prefix is its type and the base asset name is its group. Prefixes and texture suffixes (_D, _N, _ORM…) are skipped, so SM_Rock, T_Rock_D and M_Rock are all about Rock — and 15 or more of them get their own folder (guide rule 2.7). The guide sets no maximum per folder; 50 here is an opinion, and both limits are warnings because the guide says "should", not "must". Source/ is C++, not assets, and is read with the limits of c-cpp. In Content/ a folder named Assets, Meshes, Textures or Materials is a warning (type-folders, guide rule 2.6); Animations, Audio and MaterialLibrary are folders the guide itself names (2.7, 2.8).

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `warn` `{"max":50,"count":"modules"}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":15,"dropPrefix":false,"hint":"Allar 2.7: \"If you find yourself having 15+ of these assets that belong together, they should be together.\"","hintFor":["*.{uasset,umap}"]}`
- **Leading words skipped:** `u`, `i`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf,riv,lottie,caf,aiff,heic,glb,gltf,fbx,obj,tga,ktx2}`, `/Saved`, `/Intermediate`, `/DerivedDataCache`, `/Binaries`, `Content/Developers`, `__ExternalActors__`, `__ExternalObjects__`, `.vs`
- **In `**/Content`, `**/Content/**`:** `type-folders` `warn` `{"hint":"Allar 2.6.2: \"Creating a folder named Meshes, Textures, or Materials is redundant.\""}`. Allar's guide names assets, which live in Content/: the type prefix (SM_, T_, BP_) and the texture suffix (_D, _N) are not what an asset is about. In Source/ the same words are C++ (AIController).
- **In `**/Source`, `**/Source/**`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`, `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"min":5,"hint":"In C a shared prefix is often the subsystem's namespace: move them only if the subsystem deserves a directory.","hintFor":["*.{c,h,cc,cpp,cxx,hh,hpp,hxx,inl}"]}`. The 15 of Allar's rule 2.7 is about assets that belong together; C++ is code, and takes the limits of the c-cpp preset (20 modules, groups of 5).

Sources:

- [Google C++ style guide: file names](https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html)
- [Unreal Engine: World Partition, actors are saved to their own individual files (One File Per Actor)](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/world-partition-in-unreal-engine)
- [Allar's UE5 style guide (1.2 asset names, 2.6, 2.7)](https://github.com/Allar/ue5-style-guide)

## godot

Godot: a scene and its script are one (player.tscn, player.gd), and so are the .import and .uid files next to an asset. Godot's guide asks to keep resources close to the scenes that use them — folders by feature — so numbered frames (run_01.png … run_24.png) are one animation, not 24 modules. .godot and addons/ (third-party resources, in the guide's words) are left out; `crowded-folders init` lists the addons it finds and writes one exclusion for each, so that your own plugins can be checked by deleting their line. An .import or .uid file without its asset is an error (orphan-companions), and a folder named textures/, materials/ or meshes/ a warning (type-folders): the guide groups assets by what uses them and names no type folder, so this is read from it, not quoted.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`orphan-companions`:** `error`
- **`type-folders`:** `warn` `{"names":["!assets"],"hint":"Godot's guide: 'group assets as close to scenes as possible'."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `warn` `{"min":15,"hint":"Godot's guide groups assets \"as close to scenes as possible\" and gives no number: the 15 is borrowed from Allar's Unreal guide (rule 2.7) and is an opinion here."}`
- **Companions:** `_\d+$`
- **Left out:** `!*.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,svg,webp,avif,ico,icns,bmp,tif,tiff,psd,xcf,exr,hdr,mp3,wav,ogg,flac,m4a,aac,mp4,webm,mov,avi,mkv,ttf,otf,woff,woff2,eot,pdf,riv,lottie,caf,aiff,heic,glb,gltf,fbx,obj,tga,ktx2}`, `.godot`, `/addons`

Sources:

- [Godot: project organization](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/best_practices/project_organization.html)
- [Allar's UE5 style guide, rule 2.7: the number 15 is borrowed from it, Godot's guide gives none](https://github.com/Allar/ue5-style-guide)
- [Godot 4.4: .uid files](https://godotengine.org/article/uid-changes-coming-to-godot-4-4/)
- [Godot: import process, "Make sure to commit these files to your version control system, as these files contain important metadata"](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/import_process.html)

## bazel

Bazel: a folder with a BUILD.bazel is a package, with its own targets and its own visibility, so a new folder is a new BUILD file and a new set of visibility rules, not just a directory (the hint says so on every folder it proposes). The limits are recommended's measured 20 (no Bazel guide gives a number), the root of every package gets the 40 of the repository root, and the bazel-* symlinks to the output are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"hint":"In Bazel a folder with a BUILD.bazel is a package: a new folder needs its own BUILD file and its own visibility."}`
- **`prefix-groups`:** `error` `{"hint":"In Bazel a folder with a BUILD.bazel is a package: a new folder needs its own BUILD file and its own visibility."}`

## protobuf

Protocol Buffers: user.proto produces user_pb2.py, user_pb2_grpc.py, user_pb.ts, user_grpc_pb.js, user_connect.ts and user_grpc.pb.go, and all of them are the module user. Add it next to the preset of the language that holds the generated code. Proto files follow Buf's layout: a folder per package, one level of folders per package segment.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Companions:** `_(?:grpc_web_pb|grpc_pb|pb2_grpc|pb2|pb|grpc|connect)$`

- [Protocol Buffers, Python generated code: "The extension (.proto) is replaced with _pb2.py"](https://protobuf.dev/reference/python/python-generated/)

## docs

Documentation and content sites (Docusaurus, MkDocs, VitePress, Starlight, Astro, Hugo, Jekyll): number prefixes order pages and are not a group, and moving a page changes its URL, so groups in docs/, doc/, content/ and blog/ are warnings that say so; the code next to them keeps its rules. A blog's posts are a dated collection, not a drawer: _posts/, blog/ and content/posts are left as they are. Versioned copies, translations and build output are left out.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **Left out:** `versioned_docs`, `versioned_sidebars`, `/i18n`, `.docusaurus`, `/site`, `/build`, `resources/_gen`
- **In `**/docs`, `**/docs/**`, `**/doc`, `**/doc/**`, `**/content`, `**/content/**`, `**/blog`, `**/blog/**`:** `prefix-groups` `warn` `{"hint":"Moving pages changes their URLs: add redirects."}`. A page is a URL: grouping pages into a folder breaks links unless redirects are added, so it is a warning that says so.
- **In `**/_posts`, `**/_drafts`, `**/blog`, `**/content/posts`, `**/content/blog`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. A blog is a dated collection ("YEAR-MONTH-DAY-title" in Jekyll): it is read by date, not arranged by name, and it grows by design.

## data-science

Data science projects laid out like cookiecutter-data-science: notebooks/ is flat and ordered by step (1.0-initials-description.ipynb), so it is not asked to split; data, models and figures are artefacts and are left out; the package under src/ reads as Python.

- **Extends:** [python](#python)
- **Left out:** `/data`, `/models`, `reports/figures`, `/references`, `.ipynb_checkpoints`
- **In `notebooks`, `notebooks/**`:** `max-files` `off`, `prefix-groups` `off`. Notebooks are numbered by step and kept flat on purpose: the number is the order.

Sources:

- [Cookiecutter Data Science: opinions and notebook naming](https://cookiecutter-data-science.drivendata.org/opinions/)

## latex

LaTeX books and theses: chapters stay together, figures get more room (many per chapter is normal) and fig-ch3-* files grouping into figures/ch3 is a warning. Build output is left out. An opinion: LaTeX has no guide on folders.

- **Extends:** [recommended](#recommended)
- **`max-files`:** `error` `{"max":20,"count":"modules"}`
- **Left out:** `_minted*`, `svg-inkscape`, `/build`, `/out`
- **In `**/figures`, `**/figs`, `**/images`, `**/img`:** `max-files` `error` `{"max":40}`, `prefix-groups` `warn`. Many figures per chapter is normal.

Sources:

- [LaTeX Beginner's Guide: splitting a document into files](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/latex-beginners-guide/9781847199867/ch10.html)
